synopsis: Off-road braking depends on soil-mediated shear, sinkage, rolling resistance, slip and directional response; a ground model may therefore need friction, cohesion, compaction, rutting, moisture and roughness rather than merely visual terrain [f6005, f3960, f4300]. Some single-wheel semi-empirical studies report force errors below 10%, but the cited 2023 tuning varies with slip angle, and the validation evidence is limited to single-wheel rigs and sand rather than full machines [f6462, f6466, f6012]. The booklet found no published terramechanics validation adequate for braking-distance prediction across 100+ site types, but explicitly notes that Project Chrono validation literature was not reviewed; documented simulator capabilities do not establish machine-specific emergency-stopping accuracy [f10611, f6016]. Higher-fidelity CRM terrain reportedly runs 50–200 times slower than real time and requires an NVIDIA GPU, while uncertain soil inputs can overwhelm model fidelity; no evidence was found that DEM, SPH or FEM is required for automatic-braking threshold prediction across production machines [f8499, f8500, f6104, f6102]. The recommended approach is physical low-speed testing across hard, loose and wet surfaces for each machine family, conservative deceleration envelopes where transferable, and richer offline or detailed soil models only where necessary, retaining physical brake tests to address machine-ground uncertainty [f13724, f6151, f6075, f10613].
